summary: The curated subset is internally strong and fail-closed overall, with bounded inconsistencies in config discovery and untrusted diagnostic handling. No critical or high-severity defect is established by the packet.

findings.title: Config discovery conflates config and source extensions
findings.evidence: This line applies the same eight-extension set, including .jsx and .tsx, to Playwright config and spec discovery. The included playwright-debugger contract instead identifies six default config filenames at line 289, so environment detection can select a file the documented default runner would not discover.
findings.recommendation: Define separate extension sets: the six documented default Playwright config extensions and the eight supported source/spec extensions; consider other config paths only when an approved command explicitly selects them.

findings.title: Output template requests a raw artifact error
findings.evidence: The finding template labels the Error field as a raw error message, conflicting with the same skill's untrusted-artifact boundary and its bundled reader's redact-before-output contract. Directly supplied or bypassed error text could therefore be echoed with credentials or hostile terminal content intact.
findings.recommendation: Require a quoted, bounded, sanitized error excerpt and prohibit raw artifact-derived output regardless of how the error was supplied.

findings.title: Untrusted title is used as a glob pattern
findings.evidence: The guidance interpolates a report-derived test title into find -path. Shell quoting prevents command substitution but does not neutralize glob metacharacters in the title, so an attacker-controlled title can broaden or redirect artifact selection within the media root.
findings.recommendation: Enumerate validated regular media files and correlate them through structured report metadata or exact component comparison; never treat a test title as a find glob.

limitations: This packet-only review did not execute scripts or verify runtime behavior.
Omitted tests, holdouts, benchmarks, reports, repository history, and non-selected files were not used or assessed.
The result is not full product coverage, skill-accuracy evidence, independent ground truth, sealed human review, or remote model attestation.
